Brian GOULD VERSCHOYLE.

Applied for membership of the Communist Party in July, 1931. He was employed as an engineer apprentice at the works of the English Electric Company in Stafford, where he had come from Donegal in 1929. He was described by the Staffordshire Police as a studious but reticent young man, who spent most of his spare time reading Russian and Communist literature. In 1933 Brian GOULD-VERSCHOYLE was appointed organiser of the Stafford Branch of the Communist Party.

In May, 1935 he was granted a Tourist visa for Moscow, but there is no confirmation that he actually went to Russia at this stage.

At the beginning of November, 1935 Brian GOULD-VERSCHOYLE changed his address to 9 Lawn Road, Hampstead, N.W.3. (i.e. the address recorded in PIECK's note-book). He was associating at this time with Margaret C. MOOS, a Jewish refugee from Germany, and Theodor HEINISCH, an Austrian clerk from Vienna. His employment was not known. He kept irregular hours, sometimes leaving his house, where he spent a good part of his time, between 4 and 5 a.m. in the morning. He made frequent journeys to the Provinces.

According to KRIVITSKY, Paul HARDT, when he came to this country to take over the control of the Foreign Office agent KING from PIECK, rented a house in which KING used to deposit the documents he had taken from the Foreign Office. Brian GOULD-VERSCHOYLE used to collect these documents from the house and hand them over to HARDT. KRIVITSKY insisted that Brian GOULD-VERSCHOYLE thought that these documents concerned political matters, and was extremely shocked when on one occasion he accidentally discovered that the package contained Foreign Office secret documents.

Since it was not until February 1936 that Paul HARDT came to the U.K. to take over the handling of KING from PIECK, Brian GOULD-VERSCHOYLE could only have acted as intermediary for a very short time. On 11th February, 1936, Special Branch reported that Brian GOULD-VERSCHOYLE was expected to leave England in about a week's time to take up a position on the Continent.
